7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: He stepped forward but didn't sit. His hands were resting behind his back.

11.speaker: Hugo Toras
11.text: "I assume this is Manus Sazon whispering in your ear again?"

12.speaker: Hugo Toras
12.text: "I assume this is the Rizian People's Party whispering in your ear again?"
12.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Manus_Gone"] == false) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.HouseOfDelegates_Abolished"] == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Reform_DeclareIntention_Public"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_RD_Welfare_ElectoralReform"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Hugo_DecreeCounsel_LandOwnersTax"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Hugo_DecreeCounsel_InheritanceTax"] == true)

13.speaker: Hugo Toras
13.text: "So this is the trade, then? Dismantle their so-called democracy with one hand and toss them a printing press with the other?"

15.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll

16.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
16.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Vina_DancedWithManus"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_VinaManus_Approve"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_VinaManus_ApproveAfterPales"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Reform_DeclareIntention_Public"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_RD_Welfare_ElectoralReform"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Hugo_DecreeCounsel_LandOwnersTax"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Hugo_DecreeCounsel_InheritanceTax"] == true) == false

17.speaker: Hugo Toras
17.text: "Don't tell me it's that radical Sotelato who's whispering in your ear."
17.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Manus_Gone"] == false) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.HouseOfDelegates_Abolished"] == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Reform_DeclareIntention_Public"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_RD_Welfare_ElectoralReform"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Hugo_DecreeCounsel_LandOwnersTax"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Hugo_DecreeCounsel_InheritanceTax"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Reform_Movement_Leader_Adarfo"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Adarfo_Arrested"] == false  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Adarfo_Executed"] == false)

18.speaker: Hugo Toras
18.text: "I don't approve of this decree in principle..."

19.speaker: Hugo Toras
19.text: "So, you shut their mouths in the Delegate chamber but let them reach a larger audience in the streets."

20.speaker: Player_Romus
20.text: "You give them too much credit, Hugo. My decisions are my own."

21.speaker: Hugo Toras
21.text: "So this is the trade, then? Get rid of their leaders with one hand and toss them a printing press with the other?"

29.speaker: Player_Romus
29.text: "You give him too much credit, Hugo. My decisions are my own."

30.speaker: Player_Romus
30.text: "And if it were? Does that make the idea wrong, or are you just opposed to it because of who supports it?"

31.speaker: Player_Romus
31.text: "Yes, Hugo, they've infiltrated the palace and now control my every move. I suspect they're hiding under my desk as we speak."

32.speaker: Player_Romus
32.text: "If giving the people something they want prevents greater unrest, then does it matter whose idea it was first?"

33.speaker: Player_Romus
33.text: "This is about modernizing Rizia, ensuring our people have access to information beyond what the state allows."

45.speaker: Player_Romus
45.text: "Have you not seen the growing reform movement? This is what the people are demanding."

46.speaker: Player_Romus
46.text: "Have you not seen the unrest on the streets? We have to listen to the people to calm the situation."

51.speaker: Hugo Toras
51.text: "Tell me, Your Majesty, what do you think happens the moment you allow 'free press' to operate unchecked?"

52.speaker: Hugo Toras
52.text: "I oppose it because I know what will follow it. Permit the media to criticize you, and the RPP will only be the first to jump at the opportunity."

53.speaker: Hugo Toras
53.text: "Mock all you like, but it won't be so funny when their words start carrying more weight than ours."

54.speaker: Hugo Toras
54.text: "I've also seen what happens when rulers mistake concessions for control."

55.speaker: Hugo Toras
55.text: "It matters if the *gift* you're giving them will one day be used to tear down the Crown."

57.speaker: Player_Romus
57.text: "Change, Hugo. The kind we can guide, or the kind that will happen without us."

61.speaker: Hugo Toras
61.text: "But I can't help but notice that this decree was first proposed by the Rizian People's Party."

65.speaker: Player_Romus
65.text: "The same thing that happens when it's kept under a lock and key. People will find a way to speak. At least this way, I can see what they're saying."

66.speaker: Hugo Toras
66.text: "I am worried, Romus. You've already thrown your weight behind the reform movement."

68.speaker: Hugo Toras
68.text: "Tell me, Romus, will that really make them easier to control?"

69.speaker: Hugo Toras
69.text: "So, you shut down their leadership but let them reach a larger audience in the streets."

70.speaker: Hugo Toras
70.text: "Or maybe it would be like giving your enemies a megaphone. An invitation to the radicals and demagogues to undermine you in broad daylight."

71.speaker: Hugo Toras
71.text: "And for what? The illusion of transparency? The satisfaction of appeasing the RPP?"

72.speaker: Hugo Toras
72.text: "May I speak freely on this subject?"

82.speaker: Narrator
82.text: He exhaled slowly, as if holding back his immediate thoughts.

83.speaker: Hugo Toras
83.text: "But I suspect that after your move against the opposition, giving them the means to reach a larger audience may backfire."

84.speaker: Player_Romus
84.text: "You were the one who advised me to move against Manus, Hugo."

91.speaker: Hugo Toras
91.text: "This is an invitation to the radicals and demagogues to undermine you in broad daylight."

95.speaker: Player_Romus
95.text: "Just to be clear. I did not declare my full support. It was a strategic decision."

97.speaker: Player_Romus
97.text: "Let them undermine us, Hugo. The people who shout out their opinions are far less dangerous than the ones who whisper behind our backs."

98.speaker: Player_Romus
98.text: "Maybe you're right. I'm prepared to hold off on this decree."

103.speaker: Player_Romus
103.text: "Not everyone is a radical or demagogue, Hugo. But if we silence them completely, it will only grow the radicalism more. Let's listen instead of suppressing them."

104.speaker: Player_Romus
104.text: "A King who cannot face criticism is no King at all. I must take the risk."

105.speaker: Hugo Toras
105.text: "This is a dangerous game, Romus. But one you seem eager to play."

106.speaker: Narrator
106.text: He shook his head slightly. After a brief pause, he nodded.

107.speaker: Hugo Toras
107.text: "If that's the path you're set on, then so be it."

110.speaker: Hugo Toras
110.text: "Even if that's the case, your words offered them hope, and made the nobility uneasy."

111.speaker: Hugo Toras
111.text: "You didn't just support the movement, but validated it. The nobility is very concerned about this."

112.speaker: Hugo Toras
112.text: "I am worried that this will antagonize our fellow Houses against you -- and what you're trying to do..."

113.speaker: Narrator
113.text: He bowed and left the room.

115.speaker: Narrator
115.text: I took a look at the decree.

117.speaker: Hugo Toras
117.text: "Very well... I truly hope you're ready for this."

119.speaker: Player_Romus
119.text: "You've given me a lot to consider. I'll hold off on the decree for now."

121.speaker: Narrator
121.text: I gave him the unsigned decree and ended our meeting.

122.speaker: Hugo Toras
122.text: "So tell me, if I am to stand beside you in what comes next…"

123.speaker: Hugo Toras
123.text: "Are you really prepared to face that?"

124.speaker: Player_Romus
124.text: "I didn't rise to this throne to be ruled by them. I will not be the one to kneel."

126.speaker: Narrator
126.text: He looked at me with expecting eyes.

127.speaker: Player_Romus
127.text: "You're bringing up the other Houses again to warn me? Enough of this, Hugo."

131.speaker: Player_Romus
131.text: "I am. And I'd be grateful to have my Grand Vizier standing behind me."

132.speaker: Player_Romus
132.text: "I thought you wanted to speak freely, Hugo. Don't play mind games with me. Just say it."

133.speaker: Hugo Toras
133.text: "Well, you know what I think, Romus."

134.speaker: Hugo Toras
134.text: "I am against this decree. And I am against working with the RPP."

135.speaker: Hugo Toras
135.text: "But I will speak of this no more. I will support you in whatever you decide to do."

137.speaker: Player_Romus
137.text: "Maybe you're right. I'm prepared to hold off on this decree."

138.speaker: Player_Romus
138.text: "I'm warning you, Hugo. I hope you're not thinking of anything rash."

140.speaker: Hugo Toras
140.text: "Fine. I will speak of this no more."

141.speaker: Hugo Toras
141.text: "This decree is an invitation to the radicals and demagogues to undermine you in broad daylight."

142.speaker: Hugo Toras
142.text: "Rash? I am the Grand Vizier, Romus. Your uncle. If I cannot question your path, then who can?"

143.speaker: Narrator
143.text: I ignored him and took a look at the decree.

144.speaker: Hugo Toras
144.text: "I serve this House and this throne, as I always have. I do not need to prove that to you."

145.speaker: Hugo Toras
145.text: "It is not just the Houses, Romus."

147.speaker: Player_Romus
147.text: "You make it sound like charity. I prefer to think of it as balance. Let them vent, let them shout. It's easier to rule those who believe they still have choices."

148.speaker: Player_Romus
148.text: "Their democracy was a shadow play. I simply turned on the lights."

149.speaker: Player_Romus
149.text: "I just removed a liability. Now the people can truly speak their minds, not just repeat the words of their puppetmasters."

152.speaker: Player_Romus
152.text: "So, this time you're not here to warn me?"

156.speaker: Player_Romus
156.text: "Illusions can be useful, Hugo. Let them believe they have a voice. It costs me nothing, and it keeps them from demanding more."

161.speaker: Player_Romus
161.text: "Power has never been about volume. They can shout all they want in the papers, as long as they remember by whose grace they are printed."

162.speaker: Player_Romus
162.text: "Exactly. And what is your opinion on this matter?"

163.speaker: Player_Romus
163.text: "And what would you have me do instead, Hugo? Silence them entirely?"

170.speaker: Player_Romus
170.text: "Have you not seen the growing reform movement? We have to give something back to the people to calm the situation."

171.speaker: Player_Romus
171.text: "Have you not seen the unrest on the streets? We have to give something back to the people to calm the situation."

172.speaker: Hugo Toras
172.text: "It's a bold move indeed. But I disagree that we *have to*.

177.speaker: Hugo Toras
177.text: "No. I think it's a bold move."

179.speaker: Hugo Toras
179.text: "They lose their loudest voices, but gain some in the papers. You're giving them the illusion of power, while keeping it away from them."

180.speaker: Hugo Toras
180.text: "They lose their voice in government, but gain some in the papers. You're giving them the illusion of power, while keeping it away from them."

181.speaker: Player_Romus
181.text: "A little chaos, perhaps. A few angry columns, a few smug intellectuals thinking they've won something."

183.speaker: Player_Romus
183.text: "Let me guess. You believe the streets will rise and the monarchy will crumble overnight. Or, perhaps, people will just read the news over breakfast and carry on with their lives."

184.speaker: Player_Romus
184.text: "What happens? We let people speak. That's all. Not every decision is a step toward revolution, Hugo."

185.speaker: Player_Romus
185.text: "Illusions can be useful in times of growing radicalism. Let them believe they have a voice. It costs me nothing, and it hopefully keeps them from demanding more."

186.speaker: Player_Romus
186.text: "Of course they'll be antagonized. They were antagonized the moment I was crowned and refused to be their puppet."

187.speaker: Player_Romus
187.text: "You didn't protest when I got rid of Mr. Sotelato, now, did you?"

188.speaker: Player_Romus
188.text: "The movement grew radical because I followed your advice to get rid of Mr. Sazon."

189.speaker: Player_Romus
189.text: "We are long past that stage. We're already losing control over the streets."

190.speaker: Player_Romus
190.text: "The House of Delegates is already abolished, Hugo. This isn't helpful."

198.speaker: Player_Romus
198.text: "Neither is truly controllable, Hugo. But I can still guide what's happening."

199.speaker: Player_Romus
199.text: "Giving them a platform to rant instead of going out to the streets *is* control."

205.speaker: Hugo Toras
205.text: "Just think about it. This would be an invitation to radicals and demagogues to undermine you in broad daylight."

206.speaker: Hugo Toras
206.text: "But I didn't think you'd now give them the chance to reveal to everyone how the Crown moved against their leader."

208.speaker: Hugo Toras
208.text: "But I still think this will be an invitation to the radicals and demagogues to undermine you in broad daylight."

209.speaker: Player_Romus
209.text: "As if I could keep you from doing so."

210.speaker: Player_Romus
210.text: "Ironically, no. I don't want to hear your opinion on this subject. I've already made up my mind."

211.speaker: Player_Romus
211.text: "On the contrary, this is about giving citizens the illusion of power while keeping them under our control."

212.speaker: Hugo Toras
212.text: "Your words in public were... careful. But you offered them hope, and made the nobility uneasy."

214.speaker: Hugo Toras
214.text: "You're too young to remember the Voice of Rizia. But I do."

215.speaker: Hugo Toras
215.text: "Its writers didn't only attack the King's policies. They went after his personal life... even his family members."
